definition_zh: 安眠；休息；平静；安放；信赖
definition_en: a state of rest or calm sleep, or to lie resting quietly on something
core_image: 一个人平躺在草地上，动也不动，呼吸很轻
scene: 午后书房里，来访的学者在靠窗的躺椅上沉沉睡去。The old books repose on dusty shelves, untouched for years.
sceneCN: 这里 repose 是「安放、静卧」（第 3 个义项，指某物安放在某处）；句意为旧书安放在积尘的书架上，多年无人翻动。

pos.zh: 名词：安眠；休息；平静；镇静
动词：静卧；安放；休息；依赖；信赖

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「宁静的；使人安睡的」
由本词加名词后缀 -al 构成，义为「安放；休息；信赖」
由 reposed 加 -ly 构成，义为「安然地；平静地」
由 reposeful 加 -ness 构成，义为「安详；宁静」

senses.title: A state of rest or sleep
senses.definition: a condition of quiet rest, especially quiet sleep
senses.definitionCN: 安静休息的状态，尤指安静的睡眠
senses.example: She lay in quiet repose after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 长途步行之后，她静静地躺着休息。
senses.why: Re- means back, and Latin pausare means to stop; repose is the setting down of the body, the pause after effort.
senses.whyCN: re- 表示「回」，拉丁语 pausare 表示「停止」；repose 就是把身体放回去，是劳累之后的停顿。

senses.title: Calmness of a face or manner
senses.titleCN: 面容或举止的平静；安详
senses.definition: peaceful stillness in a face or behaviour, especially when nothing is happening
senses.definitionCN: 面容或举止上的安宁静止，尤其在没有动作的时候
senses.example: In repose, his face looked younger and softer.
senses.exampleCN: 静止不笑的时候，他的面容显得更年轻、更柔和。
senses.why: The face at rest is the clearest picture of repose: all movement is gone, and the calm shows itself.
senses.whyCN: 静止的脸是 repose 最清楚的画面：动作全停了，宁静就显出来。

senses.title: To lie or rest on something
senses.definition: to lie still and be supported by a surface or a place
senses.definitionCN: 静止地躺着，由某个表面或位置支撑
senses.example: Old letters repose in a wooden box under the bed.
senses.exampleCN: 旧信件安放在床下的木箱里。
senses.why: The word moves from the sleeper to ordinary things: whatever is left still and is supported by something is said to repose there.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从睡着的人扩展到普通物体：凡是被静置下来、由某物支撑的东西，都可以说 repose 在那里。

senses.title: To rest by lying down
senses.definition: to place oneself at rest, usually on a bed, a seat or the ground
senses.definitionCN: 让自己躺下休息，通常是在床、座椅或地面上
senses.example: They reposed in the shade until the worst of the heat passed.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在阴凉处歇息，直到最热的时候过去。
senses.why: As a verb the noun turns into the action: to take that pause, to lie down and let the body go quiet.
senses.whyCN: 名词化为动词，指把「停顿」这个动作做出来：躺下，让身体安静下来。

senses.title: To rest upon or depend on
senses.definition: to be founded on something or to put trust in it
senses.definitionCN: 建立在某事物之上，或把信任寄托于某事物
senses.example: Their hopes reposed on a single promising season.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的希望全寄托在一个有希望的季节上。
senses.why: Something that rests on a support is held up by it; by the same picture, hope and trust rest on their object.
senses.whyCN: 靠着支撑物的东西由它托住；同样的画面下，希望与信任也「靠」在它们的对象上。

senses.title: Composure and self-control
senses.definition: a calm, steady manner that does not get excited
senses.definitionCN: 平静稳定、不轻易激动的举止
senses.example: A scholar should meet bad news with perfect repose.
senses.exampleCN: 学者面对坏消息应当保持十足的镇定。
senses.why: If the body can rest, the mind can rest too, and repose comes to name the inner composure that shows in a quiet bearing.
senses.whyCN: 身体能安歇，心也能安歇；repose 由此指那种表现在安静姿态里的内在镇定。

intro.en: Repose joins Latin re-, back, with pausare, to pause, and has also been influenced by Latin ponere, to place.
intro.cn: repose 由拉丁语 re-（回）与 pausare（暂停）结合而成，也受到拉丁语 ponere（放置）的影响。

items.en: Pausare means to stop, pause or cease, and it is the everyday verb behind the rest sense.
items.cn: pausare 意为停止、暂停或中止，是「休息」这一含义背后的常用动词。

items.en: Re- adds the idea of back or again, so the combined sense is a pausing after activity, a settling back down.
items.cn: re- 带「回、再」之意，合起来就是活动之后的一次停顿、重新沉静下来。

items.en: The Latin verb reponere, to put back or lay a thing down, also shaped the verb, and some sources derive the placing sense from it.
items.cn: 拉丁语 reponere（放回、放下）也影响了这个动词，一些资料认为「安放」义由此而来。

items.en: Old French repaus and its verb carried the word to England, where it first meant rest and relief from labour.
items.cn: 古法语的 repaus 及其动词把这词带到英格兰，最初指休息与脱离劳作。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word had stretched to calmness of mind and to things lying still on a surface.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词已扩展到内心的平静，以及物体静置于某表面。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on Latin pausare or ponere; the near-meaning group gathers words about rest, sleep and stillness.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁语 pausare 或 ponere 构成的词；近义组收表示休息、睡眠与静止的词，语义范围各有不同。

entries.definition: A short stop made before continuing; built on the same Latin pausare.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「暂停、停顿」，与 repose 同出拉丁语 pausare。

entries.definition: To put parts together or to calm oneself; the ending looks alike but it comes from Latin ponere, to place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「组成、创作、使镇定」，词尾与 repose 相近，但来自拉丁语 ponere（放置）。

entries.definition: To put forward a plan or suggestion; it shares the ending of the placing family, not the pausing family.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提议、提出」，属「放置」一族而非「暂停」一族，与 repose 只是词尾相近。

entries.definition: The plain everyday word for stopping work and relaxing; broader and less literary than repose.
entries.definitionCN: 最常见表示「休息」的词，范围更宽、语体更口语，不如 repose 书面。

entries.definition: The natural state of unconsciousness at night; a narrower and more ordinary word.
entries.definitionCN: 夜间自然失去意识的状态，义域更窄、更日常，不如 repose 含「安详」意味。

entries.definition: A deep inner calm; it names the feeling, while repose names the posture of rest.
entries.definitionCN: 深层的内心宁静；serenity 指感受本身，repose 更强调休息的姿态。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin sources pausare, to pause, and ponere, to place, and the common phrases of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁来源 pausare（暂停）与 ponere（放置），以及这个词的常见搭配。

normal.en: Re- means back and pausare means to pause, so repose is the pause that comes after effort.
normal.cn: re- 表示「回」，pausare 表示「暂停」，所以 repose 是劳累之后的那次停顿。

normal.en: The same pausare gives pause, so a repose is a long and quiet pause.
normal.cn: 同一个 pausare 还给出 pause，所以 repose 就是一次漫长而安静的暂停。

normal.en: The ending of repose recalls ponere, to place, which is why things also repose on shelves.
normal.cn: repose 的词尾让人想到 ponere（放置），所以物品也能 repose 在架子上。

normal.en: In repose is a fixed phrase for the still, calm state, usually of a face or a body.
normal.cn: in repose 是固定的搭配，指静止平静的状态，常用于形容面容或身体。

normal.en: The reverse order gives the verb repose on, meaning both to rest on and to depend on.
normal.cn: 倒过来组成短语 repose on，既表示「安放在……上」，也表示「依赖于」。

abstract.en: Picture a figure lying flat in tall grass, arms open, not moving at all.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人平躺在深草里，手臂摊开，一动也不动。

abstract.en: Look at a sleeping face: every muscle is still, and the stillness itself shows calm.
abstract.cn: 看一眼睡着的脸：每块肌肉都停了，而这份静止本身就显出平静。

abstract.en: Think of heavy books resting on a shelf that holds them up; their weight is trusted to the wood.
abstract.cn: 想象厚书安放在支撑它们的书架上；它们的重量被托付给了木板。

examples.en: The patient finally found a few hours of repose after the noisy night.
examples.cn: 经历嘈杂的一夜之后，病人终于获得了几个小时的安眠。

examples.en: The village reposes beside a quiet river under a warm sun.
examples.cn: 村庄静卧在暖阳下一条安静的小河旁。

examples.en: Her argument reposes on evidence that has never been checked.
examples.cn: 她的论证建立在从未被核实过的证据之上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞剖兹」——把身子重新放平，安歇下来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）+ pausare（暂停、停止）→ repose（休息、停顿），并受 ponere（放置）影响形成「安放」义；古法语 repaus 传入英语，核心义「停止动作、把身体放回安宁」。

sensesIntro.en: Repose begins with the body at rest, moves to the calm that rests on a face, then to things lying still, to lying down oneself, to trust resting on an object, and finally to inner composure.
sensesIntro.cn: repose 从身体安歇开始，转到停在脸上的平静，再到物品静置、自己躺下歇息、信任寄托于某物，最后落到内心的镇定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure lies flat on the grass, perfectly still, breathing slowly.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人平躺在草地上，完全静止，呼吸缓慢。

branches.en: THE BODY: stopping effort and lying down is the core act, whether named by the noun or the verb.
branches.cn: 身体线：停止用力、躺下来是核心动作，名词与动词都指这一点。

branches.en: THE FACE: a still face shows the calm directly, so repose names the look of rest.
branches.cn: 面容线：静止的脸直接显出平静，repose 因此指「休息时的样子」。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: anything left still and supported is said to repose on its surface.
branches.cn: 物件线：任何被静置并被支撑的东西，都说 repose 在其表面。

branches.en: THE SUPPORT: what rests on something is upheld by it, so hope and trust can repose on a person or a plan.
branches.cn: 支撑线：靠在某物上的东西由它托住，于是希望与信任可以 repose 在某人或某计划上。

branches.en: THE MIND: inner composure is the stillness of the body carried inside.
branches.cn: 内心线：内在的镇定就是身体的静止被带进了心里。

intro.en: Repose is a Latin prefix plus a pausing root, with words from Latin ponere, to place, shaping its second family of meanings.
intro.cn: repose 是拉丁前缀加「暂停」词根构成，而来自拉丁语 ponere（放置）的词则塑造了它的第二组含义。

latinIntro.en: Latin pausare means to pause, and ponere means to place; both are recorded, so only the earlier forms are reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pausare 意为暂停，ponere 意为放置；两者均有文献记录，只有更早的形式属于重构。

items.example: The prefix points to a return to stillness.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀指向回到安静。

items.example: The verb supplies the pause in repose.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 repose 中「暂停」那一层。

items.example: The placing root lies behind the sense to lay down.
items.exampleCN: 「放置」词根支撑着「放下」这一含义。

items.example: The suffix -al forms reposal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 reposal。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms reposeful.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 构成 reposeful。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms reposefulness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 reposefulness。

items.example: Reposeful describes a peaceful scene.
items.exampleCN: reposeful 描述宁静的景象。

items.example: Compose comes from ponere with a different prefix.
items.exampleCN: compose 由 ponere 换一个前缀构成。

items.example: Pause is the plain word beside repose.
items.exampleCN: pause 是 repose 旁边的普通说法。

definition_zh: 击退；打退；排斥；使反感；拒绝
definition_en: to drive back an attacking force, to make a person feel strong dislike, or to refuse an offer or a request firmly
core_image: 一堵看不见的墙在伸手的人面前突然推开，把靠近的东西原路送回
scene: 海滩上，救生员第三次把游得太远的少年送回浅水区。The lifeguard repulsed the swimmer who had drifted too far from the shore.
sceneCN: 这里 repulse 是「击退」（第 1 个义项：把靠近的人或力量挡回去）；句意：救生员把游得太远的游泳者挡了回来。

pos.zh: 击退；打退；排斥；使反感；拒绝
击退；败退；拒斥

derivatives.zh: 由 repulse 加名词词尾 -ion 构成，义为「厌恶；排斥力」
由 repulse 加形容词词尾 -ive 构成，义为「令人反感的」
由 repulsive 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「令人反感地」
由 repulsive 加 -ness 构成，义为「可憎之状」

senses.title: To drive back an attacking force
senses.definition: to force an enemy or an attacking group to move back and abandon its advance
senses.definitionCN: 迫使敌人或来袭的人后退、放弃推进
senses.example: The garrison repulsed three attempts to storm the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 守军击退了三次强攻城门的企图。
senses.why: Latin re- means back and pellere means to drive, so repulse is literally the act of driving a force back from you.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 re- 表示「向后」，pellere 表示「推」，repulse 字面就是「把来犯的力量往后推」，所以最先长出军事的「击退」义。

senses.title: To fill someone with disgust
senses.definition: to cause strong dislike or a sense of disgust in someone
senses.definitionCN: 使人产生强烈的厌恶或恶心感
senses.example: The smell of the fish market repulsed her instantly.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼市的气味立刻让她感到恶心。
senses.why: The push that turns away an army turns away a person too; here the thing pushes feeling away instead of a body, so the verb means to drive someone off emotionally.
senses.whyCN: 能把军队挡开的推力也能把人挡开，只是这里挡住的是情感而非身体，于是「推回去」变成了让人心生厌恶。

senses.title: To reject a proposal flatly
senses.definition: to refuse an offer, a request, or an idea firmly and without discussion
senses.definitionCN: 坚决而干脆地拒绝提议、请求或想法
senses.example: The committee repulsed the plan without even taking a vote.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会甚至没有投票就把这个方案否掉了。
senses.why: Refusing a suggestion is also a way of pushing it back, so the same verb covers a cold refusal as well as a physical defence.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝一个建议同样是把对方递来的东西推回去，所以同一个动词既能指实体的防卫，也能指冷淡的拒绝。

senses.title: To oppose or repel a mass of people
senses.definition: to resist and hold back a crowd, a wave, or an advancing mass
senses.definitionCN: 抵挡并挡住人群、浪潮或推进的大片事物
senses.example: The barricades repulsed the crowd for most of the night.
senses.exampleCN: 路障在大半夜里一直把人群挡在外面。
senses.why: Besides soldiers, the thing driven back may be a crowd, a flock, or a tide, and the image of a wall pushing back still holds.
senses.whyCN: 被推回去的不只是军队，也可能是人群、兽群或潮水，而「一堵墙往后推」的画面始终没有变。

senses.title: A repulse as a defeat
senses.definition: the act of driving back an enemy, or the failure of an attack that is driven back
senses.definitionCN: 击退敌人的行为，或被击退的进攻失败
senses.example: The defenders celebrated the repulse of the second wave.
senses.exampleCN: 守军庆祝击退了第二波进攻。
senses.why: The verb became a noun early on, naming the event of being driven back, and modern military writing still uses it for a failed assault.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词很早就可作名词，指「被推回去」这件事，现代军事文字仍用它来指一次失败的进攻。

senses.title: Repulsion between physical bodies
senses.definition: to push two bodies or particles apart by the force that opposes attraction
senses.definitionCN: 让两个物体或粒子因与吸引力相对的力量而彼此推开
senses.example: Two electrons repulse each other as they approach.
senses.exampleCN: 两个电子靠近时会彼此排斥。
senses.why: Physics borrows the literal Latin meaning: two like charges drive each other away, which is pellere at work again.
senses.whyCN: 物理学借用了这个词的字面拉丁义：同种电荷互相推开，正是 pellere（推）在起作用。

intro.en: Repulse comes from Latin repulsus, the past participle of repellere, to drive back, built from re-, back, and pellere, to drive.
intro.cn: repulse 来自拉丁语 repulsus，即 repellere（推回）的过去分词，由 re-（向后）与 pellere（推动）构成。

items.en: Pellere means to drive, to strike, or to push away.
items.cn: pellere 意为驱动、击打、推开。

items.en: Repellere adds re- and means to drive back or to reject.
items.cn: repellere 加上 re-，意为推回、击退、拒绝。

items.en: Repulsus is the past participle meaning driven back.
items.cn: repulsus 为过去分词，意为被推回的。

items.en: English takes the participle form, not the verb stem, and spells it repulse.
items.cn: 英语取的是过去分词形式而非动词词干，写作 repulse。

items.en: The word first describes armies driven off in battle.
items.cn: 这个词最早描写的是战场上的击退。

items.en: It later names the way a sight or smell drives a person away, and the pushing apart of charges in physics.
items.cn: 后来它指景物或气味把人「逼开」，也指物理学中电荷的互斥。

note.en: Repulse belongs to the pellere family with repulsion, repel, and impulsive, and it sits beside words for disgust and refusal.
note.cn: repulse 属于 pellere 词族，与 repulsion、repel、impulsive 同源，同时也与表示厌恶和拒绝的词为邻。

entries.definition: to drive something back or to make someone feel dislike
entries.definitionCN: 击退；排斥；使厌恶（与 repulse 同源，可互换度很高）

entries.definition: a strong feeling of disgust, or a force that pushes bodies apart
entries.definitionCN: 厌恶；排斥力（名词形式）

entries.definition: acting quickly without thinking ahead
entries.definitionCN: 冲动的（同用 pellere，前缀改为 im-，意为「向内推」）

entries.definition: to make someone feel strong disapproval or nausea
entries.definitionCN: 使厌恶；使作呕

entries.definition: to fill someone with a feeling of violent dislike
entries.definitionCN: 使憎恶；使反感（语气更强烈）

entries.definition: to refuse an offer or a friendliness in an unkind, abrupt way
entries.definitionCN: 断然拒绝；冷落

normalIntro.en: Repulse is a pushing word: re- pushes back and pellere drives, so something is sent the way it came.
normalIntro.cn: repulse 是一个「推」的词：re- 往后推，pellere 是驱动，于是东西被原路送回。

normal.en: Repulse shares the root pellere with repel, propulsion, and impulse.
normal.cn: repulse 与 repel、propulsion、impulse 共用词根 pellere。

normal.en: To repulse an attack is to push it back before it reaches you.
normal.cn: repulse an attack 就是在进攻到达之前把它顶回去。

normal.en: The passive pattern be repulsed by describes disgust: She was repulsed by the sight.
normal.cn: 被动结构 be repulsed by 用于表达厌恶：她被眼前的景象恶心到了。

normal.en: The -ion form repulsion can be used at once for disgust and for the force between magnets.
normal.cn: 名词 repulsion 既能指厌恶，也能指磁铁之间的排斥力。

normal.en: Compare repulse with refuse: refuse is plain and general, repulse is stronger and suggests pushing someone away.
normal.cn: 对比 refuse：refuse 平实通用，repulse 更强，含「把人推开」之意。

abstract.en: Picture a row of shields closing against a charging horse.
abstract.cn: 想象一排盾牌合拢，挡住冲来的马。

abstract.en: Picture a hand jerking back from a hot plate.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从滚烫的盘子上猛地缩回。

abstract.en: Picture a letter of refusal pushed back across the desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一封拒绝信被推回桌面另一侧。

examples.en: The small garrison repulsed the raiders and held the bridge.
examples.cn: 小股守军击退了劫掠者，守住了桥梁。

examples.en: Many viewers were repulsed by the film and left early.
examples.cn: 许多观众被这部片子恶心到了，中途离场。

examples.en: The board repulsed every offer that would cut staff.
examples.cn: 董事会拒绝了每一个要裁员的报价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞怕死」——谐音近似「瑞怕死」，一见敌人就怕死，反而拼命把对方推回去，就是「击退」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（向后）+ pellere（推、驱动）→ repellere（推回；击退）→ 过去分词 repulsus → 英语 repulse，核心义是「把靠近的东西推回去」。

sensesIntro.en: Repulse starts as the military act of pushing an enemy back, widens to pushing people, feelings, and offers away, and finally names the pushing force itself.
sensesIntro.cn: repulse 起于军事上把敌人推回去，随后扩展为把人、情感与提议挡开，最后连「推力」本身也一并命名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand thrust out to send an approaching thing back.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸出一只手，把靠近的东西推回去。

branches.en: Driving an army back is the original physical sense.
branches.cn: 把军队推回去是原始的实体义项。

branches.en: The same push, aimed at a person, becomes disgust.
branches.cn: 同一次推动指向人时，就成了厌恶。

branches.en: Pushing back an offer is a cold refusal.
branches.cn: 把提议推回去就是冷淡的拒绝。

branches.en: Crowds and tides are driven back just as armies are.
branches.cn: 人群与潮水也像军队一样被挡回去。

branches.en: The event of being driven back and the force that drives apart both name the push itself.
branches.cn: 「被推回」的事件与「互斥」的力，都在命名这次推动本身。

intro.en: Repulse is built on the Latin prefix re- and the root pellere, which also gives repel, repulsion, and impulsive.
intro.cn: repulse 由拉丁语前缀 re- 与词根 pellere 构成，同根词还包括 repel、repulsion 与 impulsive。

latinIntro.en: Latin pellere means to drive or to push, and repellere means to drive something back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pellere 意为驱动、推动，repellere 意为把某物推回去。

items.example: The prefix re- turns the push into a push back.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 把「推」变成「推回」。

items.example: Pellere supplies the pushing image.
items.exampleCN: pellere 提供「推」的意象。

items.example: Repellere joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: repellere 把前缀与词根合在一起。

items.meaning: to drive back or to disgust
items.example: The defenders repulse the attack.
items.exampleCN: 守军击退进攻。

items.meaning: disgust or the force of pushing apart
items.example: The suffix -ion forms repulsion.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 repulsion。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms repulsive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 repulsive。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms repulsively.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 repulsively。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms repulsiveness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 repulsiveness。

definition_zh: 令人厌恶的；反感的；排斥的；排斥性的
definition_en: arousing strong disgust or dislike, or having the power to drive something away or apart
core_image: 一股看不见的力量从身上弹开，任何靠近的东西都被原路顶回去
scene: 厨房水槽里泡了一夜的食物散发出刺鼻的臭味，全家人都躲远了。The food left in the sink overnight gave off a repulsive smell.
sceneCN: 这里 repulsive 是「令人厌恶的」（第 1 个义项：气味本身使人恶心、躲开）；句意：在水槽里泡了一夜的食物散发出令人作呕的气味。

pos.zh: 令人厌恶的；反感的；排斥的；排斥性的

derivatives.zh: 由 repulsive 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「令人反感地」
由 repulsive 加 -ness 构成，义为「可憎；令人厌恶的性质」
同源名词，义为「厌恶；排斥力」
同源动词，义为「击退；使反感」

senses.title: Causing strong disgust
senses.titleCN: 令人作呕的；令人恶心的
senses.definition: causing a strong feeling of disgust, especially through smell, texture, or appearance
senses.definitionCN: 尤指通过气味、触感或外观引起强烈的厌恶
senses.example: The wound had turned repulsive and needed prompt care.
senses.exampleCN: 伤口已经变得惨不忍睹，需要赶紧处理。
senses.why: The suffix -ive turns the verb into a quality, so the thing itself now does the pushing that makes people turn away.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ive 把动词变成一种性质，于是被推开的不再是人，而是物本身带着「把人推开」的力量。

senses.title: Very unpleasant in behaviour
senses.definition: so unpleasant or offensive that people reject the person or the conduct
senses.definitionCN: 如此令人不适或冒犯，以致人们排斥这个人或这种行为
senses.example: His repulsive jokes cleared the room in minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他那些令人反感的玩笑几分钟就让屋里的人散光了。
senses.why: What is pushed away need not be physical: conduct that drives people off is described with the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 被推开的未必是实体，令人走开的行为同样用这个形容词来描述。

senses.title: Driven away, rejected
senses.definition: describing a person or thing that has been driven back or has been rebuffed
senses.definitionCN: 形容被推回去、被断然拒绝的人或事物
senses.example: The repulsive answer ended the discussion at once.
senses.exampleCN: 那个被挡回去的答复立刻结束了讨论。
senses.why: From Latin repulsus, driven back, the adjective can still describe the one who has been turned away rather than the one who causes the turning.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 repulsus 意为「被推回的」，所以这个形容词也能形容被挡开的一方，而不只是造成排斥的一方。

senses.title: Forcing things apart
senses.definition: describing a force or a field that pushes two bodies or particles away from each other
senses.definitionCN: 形容把两个物体或粒子相互推开的力或场
senses.example: The like poles create a repulsive force between the magnets.
senses.exampleCN: 相同的磁极在两个磁铁之间产生排斥力。
senses.why: Physics keeps the literal Latin sense: a force that drives back is a force of repulsion, and the adjective names it.
senses.whyCN: 物理学保留了字面的拉丁义：一股「推回去」的力就是排斥力，形容词正用来形容它。

senses.title: Rising against an offer
senses.definition: expressed in a manner that drives a proposal or a request back without discussion
senses.definitionCN: 以一种不给讨论余地、把提议或请求推回去的方式表达
senses.example: The trade union met the pay freeze with a repulsive response.
senses.exampleCN: 工会以断然否定的态度回应了薪资冻结。
senses.why: The physical push back can be transferred to a reply, so an answer that rejects a proposal outright is called repulsive in older prose.
senses.whyCN: 实体的推回可以转移到话语上，于是在较早的书面语里，把提议直接推回去的答复也被称作 repulsive。

intro.en: Repulsive is repulse plus the Latin-derived suffix -ive, built on Latin repellere, to drive back.
intro.cn: repulsive 是 repulse 加拉丁来源的词尾 -ive 构成，其根本是拉丁语 repellere（推回）。

items.en: Pellere means to drive or to push.
items.cn: pellere 意为驱动、推动。

items.en: Repellere means to drive back or to reject.
items.cn: repellere 意为推回、击退、拒绝。

items.en: The suffix -ivus marks a quality that acts, so repulsivus is what has the power to drive back.
items.cn: 词尾 -ivus 标记能起作用的性质，因此 repulsivus 意为「有推回之力的」。

items.en: The adjective enters English as a word for driving back, and then for the quality of causing disgust.
items.cn: 这个形容词进入英语时指「推回的」，随后转为指「引起厌恶的」。

items.en: Writers use repulsive for smells, sights, and manners that people recoil from.
items.cn: 作家们用 repulsive 形容人们会闪避的气味、景象与举止。

items.en: Science fixes a technical sense for a force that pushes bodies apart.
items.cn: 科学为「把物体推开的力」锁定了一个技术义。

note.en: Repulsive sits in the pellere family next to repulse and repulsion, and it is close to the vocabulary of disgust and of physical repulsion.
note.cn: repulsive 处在 pellere 词族里，紧邻 repulse 与 repulsion，同时靠近表示厌恶和物理排斥的词。

entries.definition: to drive back or to fill someone with disgust
entries.definitionCN: 击退；使反感（动词原形）

entries.definition: a strong feeling of disgust or a force that pushes bodies apart
entries.definitionCN: 厌恶；排斥力（名词形式）

entries.definition: acting on a sudden urge without thinking
entries.definitionCN: 冲动的（同用 pellere，但前缀与词尾不同，意义也不同）

entries.definition: extremely unpleasant and likely to make someone feel sick
entries.definitionCN: 令人恶心的；使人作呕的

entries.definition: very offensive and annoying, used mainly of people and behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 讨厌的；令人反感的（多用于人的举止）

entries.definition: morally hateful and deeply unacceptable
entries.definitionCN: 令人憎恶的（正式，偏道德判断）

normalIntro.en: Repulsive is the adjective of a push back: whatever it describes makes people or particles move away.
normalIntro.cn: repulsive 是「推回」的形容词形式：凡是被它形容的东西，都会让人或粒子离开。

normal.en: Repulse plus -ive gives repulsive, the quality of driving away.
normal.cn: repulse 加 -ive 得到 repulsive，表示「把人推开的性质」。

normal.en: Repulsive is stronger than unpleasant: it suggests a physical recoil.
normal.cn: repulsive 比 unpleasant 更强，带有身体后退的意味。

normal.en: The technical pattern like poles are repulsive is common in physics texts.
normal.cn: 物理文本里常见「同极相斥」的说法，形容词用的正是这个词。

normal.en: Compare with repulsion: the noun is the feeling or the force, the adjective is the thing causing it.
normal.cn: 对比 repulsion：名词指那种感觉或那种力，形容词指造成它的东西。

normal.en: Repulsive often describes smells, textures, wounds, and conduct.
normal.cn: repulsive 常用来形容气味、触感、伤口与举止。

abstract.en: Picture two magnets refusing to snap together no matter how you push.
abstract.cn: 想象两块磁铁，无论怎么推都不肯吸在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pulling away from a slimy surface.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从黏滑的表面上缩了回去。

abstract.en: Picture a table of diners standing up and walking out at once.
abstract.cn: 想象满桌的客人一起站起来走掉。

examples.en: She found the raw fish repulsive and pushed the plate away.
examples.cn: 她觉得生鱼太恶心，把盘子推开了。

examples.en: Two like charges are mutually repulsive.
examples.cn: 同种电荷彼此排斥。

examples.en: Repulsive habits cost him his place in the team.
examples.cn: 令人反感的习惯让他失去了队里的位置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞怕硒」——谐音近似「瑞怕硒」，一闻到那股怪味就往后躲，正像被一只无形的手推回去，「令人厌恶」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（向后）+ pellere（推）+ 词尾 -ive（具有……性质的）→ 英语 repulsive，核心义是「具有把人推开之性质的」。

sensesIntro.en: Repulsive takes the pushing image and turns it into a quality: it can mean the thing that drives people off, the conduct that does so, the one pushed away, or the force that separates particles.
sensesIntro.cn: repulsive 把「推」的画面变成一种性质：可以指让人躲开的东西、让人走开的举止、被挡开的一方，也可以指把粒子分开的力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface that throws off everything that touches it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个表面把碰到它的东西都弹开。

branches.en: The quality of causing disgust is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 「令人作呕」是日常义项。

branches.en: Conduct that drives people off shares the same quality.
branches.cn: 让人走开的行为共享同一种性质。

branches.en: The one driven back may also be called repulsive in older prose.
branches.cn: 在较早的书面语里，被挡开的一方也可能被称作 repulsive。

branches.en: Disgust and the physics of repulsion both describe being pushed away.
branches.cn: 生理上的厌恶与物理上的排斥，都是在描述被推开。

branches.en: A rebuff and a rejected proposal are the social face of the same push.
branches.cn: 被人挡回与提案被否，是同一次推动在社会层面的表现。

intro.en: Repulsive combines the Latin base of repulse with the suffix -ive, and a set of English endings grows from it.
intro.cn: repulsive 由 repulse 的拉丁词基加词尾 -ive 构成，英语中还有一串词尾从它派生。

latinIntro.en: Latin pellere means to push, repellere to drive back, and the suffix -ivus marks a quality that acts.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pellere 意为推动，repellere 意为推回，词尾 -ivus 标记能起作用的性质。
