items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 提供「向后」的意思。

items.example: Pellere supplies the pushing image.
items.exampleCN: pellere 提供「推」的意象。

items.example: The suffix -ive turns the verb into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 把动词变成形容词。

items.example: The smell is repulsive.
items.exampleCN: 这气味令人作呕。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms repulsively.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 repulsively。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms repulsiveness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 repulsiveness。

items.meaning: disgust or the force of pushing apart
items.example: The suffix -ion forms repulsion.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 repulsion。

items.example: Repulse is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: repulse 是基础动词。

latinEntries.meaning: having the quality of, tending to

definition_zh: 有名望的；声誉好的；值得信赖的；正规的
definition_en: respected and trusted by other people because of a good record, and therefore taken as honest and reliable
core_image: 一块挂在门楣上的老招牌，来来往往的人都点头认可，说这家靠得住
scene: 家长挑补习班时，会先看这所机构有没有口碑好的认证。Parents check for certification from a reputable institute before enrolling their child.
sceneCN: 这里 reputable 是「声誉好的；靠得住的」（第 1 个义项：因口碑好而受人信赖）；句意：家长给孩子报名前，会先确认这家机构有信誉良好的机构认证。

pos.zh: 有名望的；声誉好的；值得信赖的；正规的

derivatives.zh: 由 repute 加名词词尾 -ation 构成，义为「名声；声誉」
由 reputable 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「名声良好地」
由 reputable 加 -ity 构成，义为「信誉；可敬之名」
基础名词，义为「名声；名誉」

senses.title: Held in good repute
senses.definition: describing a person, firm, or school that others think well of because of a solid record
senses.definitionCN: 形容因业绩扎实而被他人看重的个人、公司或学校
senses.example: She works for a reputable firm of architects in the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 她在老城区一家口碑很好的建筑师事务所工作。
senses.why: Latin reputare means to count or reckon, so reputable is short for being counted as good by others.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 reputare 意为「计算、估量」，reputable 本是「被人算计为好」的缩写，核心义就是被大家算作可取。

senses.title: Trustworthy as a source
senses.definition: describing information, evidence, or a source that can be trusted to be accurate
senses.definitionCN: 形容可以信赖其准确性的信息、证据或来源
senses.example: Only reputable journals were used for the literature review.
senses.exampleCN: 文献综述只采用了可靠的期刊。
senses.why: If others count a name as good, its words carry weight too, so the adjective moves from the owner of a name to the content that name produces.
senses.whyCN: 既然众人把某个名字算作好名，这个名字说出的话就有了分量，于是形容词从「名字的主人」转到「这个名字产出的内容」。

senses.title: Legitimate and established
senses.definition: describing a business or an organisation that operates lawfully and with a settled standing
senses.definitionCN: 形容合法经营、地位稳定扎实的企业或机构
senses.example: Always choose a reputable dealer when buying a used car.
senses.exampleCN: 买二手车时一定要选正规经销商。
senses.why: A good name is built by years of steady dealing, so reputable also tells you that a business is regular and lawful rather than shady.
senses.whyCN: 好名声靠多年规矩买卖积累，因此 reputable 也暗示这家企业正规合法，而非来路不正。

senses.title: Well thought of in a profession
senses.definition: describing a person who is well regarded among specialists in a field
senses.definitionCN: 形容在某一领域的同行中广受敬重的人
senses.example: The museum hired a reputable scholar to date the coins.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆请来一位在业内颇有声望的学者为钱币断代。
senses.why: Repute can come from a narrow circle, so the word often names standing among peers rather than fame with the public.
senses.whyCN: 名声也可以只来自一个小圈子，因此这个词常指同行之间的地位，而不是公众知名度。

senses.title: Conducted in a decent way
senses.definition: describing dealings or manners that are considered proper and honest
senses.definitionCN: 形容被认为得体、诚实的行为方式
senses.example: The club has a long record of reputable conduct towards its members.
senses.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部长期以来都体面地对待会员。
senses.why: The same reckoning extends to how people behave, so reputable also tells others that a course of action can be called decent.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「评判」也扩展到人的行为方式上，所以 reputable 也能告诉别人一条路子是体面可取的。

intro.en: Reputable comes from repute, from Latin reputare, to reckon, which joins re-, again, and putare, to count or to think.
intro.cn: reputable 来自 repute，再上溯到拉丁语 reputare（估量、计算），由 re-（再）与 putare（计算、思量）构成。

items.en: Putare means to cut, to prune, and also to reckon or to think.
items.cn: putare 意为切削、修剪，也有计算、思量的意思。

items.en: Reputare means to count up again or to consider carefully.
items.cn: reputare 意为重新计算、反复思量。

items.en: Reputatio names the result of that reckoning, namely one good name.
items.cn: reputatio 指出这种估量的结果，即名声。

items.en: Repute enters English from Old French as a noun for a name or standing.
items.cn: repute 经古法语进入英语，作名词表示名声、地位。

items.en: Reputable appears as the adjective for having a good name.
items.cn: reputable 作为「有好名声的」形容词出现。

items.en: The word is now most at home in commerce, journalism, and research.
items.cn: 如今这个词最常见于商业、新闻与研究领域。

note.en: Reputable is built on repute and shares putare with compute and dispute, and it stands close to the everyday words for trust and for fame.
note.cn: reputable 由 repute 派生，与 compute、dispute 共用 putare，并与日常的「可信」与「有名」两类词相近。

entries.definition: fame or the estimate that others have of a person
entries.definitionCN: 名声；名誉（基础名词）

entries.definition: the opinion that others hold about a person or a thing
entries.definitionCN: 名声；声誉（名词形式）

entries.definition: able to be blamed on or attributed to someone
entries.definitionCN: 可归咎于……的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: considered proper and decent by society
entries.definitionCN: 体面的；受人尊敬的

entries.definition: able to be believed because of the evidence
entries.definitionCN: 可信的（重在证据能否立得住）

entries.definition: reliable and honest enough to be trusted
entries.definitionCN: 值得信赖的（更口语）

normalIntro.en: Reputable comes from repute, to be counted, so the word means that a name adds up to good.
normalIntro.cn: reputable 来自 repute（被算计、被衡量），所以它的意思是「这个名字一算就算好」。

normal.en: Repute plus -able gives reputable: able to be reckoned good by others.
normal.cn: repute 加 -able 得到 reputable：能被别人算作好的。

normal.en: Reputable describes people and firms; reputation describes what they have.
normal.cn: reputable 形容人和公司，reputation 是它所拥有的东西。

normal.en: The pattern a reputable source is common in academic writing.
normal.cn: a reputable source 是学术写作中的常见搭配。

normal.en: Compare reputable with reputed: reputable means good, reputed only means believed to be.
normal.cn: 对比 reputed：reputable 只是「好的」，reputed 只表示「据说是」。

normal.en: Root putare, to reckon, also appears in compute and dispute.
normal.cn: 词根 putare（估量）也出现在 compute 与 dispute 里。

abstract.en: Picture an old signboard that passers-by nod at.
abstract.cn: 想象一块老招牌，路过的人都会点头。

abstract.en: Picture a lawyer whose name is printed at the top of a long letterhead.
abstract.cn: 想象一位律师的名字印在长长的信笺顶端。

abstract.en: Picture people quietly ticking the same name on a list.
abstract.cn: 想象众人悄悄在名单上把同一个名字打上钩。

examples.en: The journal is reputable, so its findings were taken seriously.
examples.cn: 这本期刊很有信誉，所以它的研究结论受到重视。

examples.en: They sold the flat through a reputable agent in the city.
examples.cn: 他们通过城里一家声誉良好的中介卖掉了公寓。

examples.en: Few reputable historians accept that story.
examples.cn: 很少有有声望的历史学家相信那个说法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞普特婆」——谐音近似「瑞普特婆」，街坊都说这位婆婆做事特别靠谱，「名声好」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再）+ putare（计算、思量）→ reputare（反复估量）→ reputatio（名声）→ 古法语 repute → 英语 repute + -able，核心义是「经众人反复估量仍算得好的」。

sensesIntro.en: Reputable begins as being counted good by others, passes on to the sources and business that carry that good name, and ends with the standing a person has among peers and the decency of a course of action.
sensesIntro.cn: reputable 起于「被众人算作好」，继而形容带着这种好名声的来源与企业，最后延伸到同行中的地位与行为的体面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name that people keep ticking as good.
core.cn: 核心意象：众人反复在心里打到勾的那个名字。

branches.en: Being counted good is the core sense of the adjective.
branches.cn: 被算作好是这个词的核心义项。

branches.en: A good name passes to the information it produces.
branches.cn: 好名声会转移到它产出的信息上。

branches.en: A steady good name marks a business as regular and lawful.
branches.cn: 稳定的好名声使企业显得正规合法。

branches.en: The reckoning may come from a whole public or from a narrow circle of peers.
branches.cn: 这种估量可以来自公众，也可以只来自一小圈同行。

branches.en: Lawful dealing and decent conduct are both a good name put into practice.
branches.cn: 合法买卖与体面行为，都是好名声落到实处的样子。

intro.en: Reputable is the root repute plus the suffix -able, and English builds a small family of nouns and adverbs around it.
intro.cn: reputable 是词根 repute 加词尾 -able，英语围绕它构成了一小族名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin reputare means to reckon up, built from re-, again, and putare, to count or to think.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 reputare 意为重新估量，由 re-（再）与 putare（计算、思量）构成。

items.example: The prefix re- gives the idea of counting again.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 带来「再数一遍」的意思。

items.example: Putare also yields compute and dispute.
items.exampleCN: putare 还衍生出 compute 与 dispute。

items.example: Reputare joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: reputare 把前缀与词根合在一起。

items.example: A writer of repute is well known and trusted.
items.exampleCN: a writer of repute 指有名望、受信任的作家。

items.example: The suffix -able forms reputable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 reputable。

items.meaning: the act or the result of
items.example: The suffix -ation forms reputation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 reputation。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms reputably.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 reputably。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms reputability.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 reputability。

definition_zh: 必需的；必不可少的；必需品；必要条件
definition_en: necessary for a particular purpose, or a thing that is needed
core_image: 一张办事清单上只有一项被红笔圈住，写着「非有不可」
scene: 招聘启事列了十几条要求，求职者一眼看去，只圈出其中必不可少的那几条。The job notice lists many wishes, but the applicant circles only the requisite skills.
sceneCN: 这里 requisite 是「必需的」（第 1 个义项：为某个目的非有不可的）；句意：招聘启事列了十几条愿望，求职者只圈出了那几项必不可少的技能。

pos.zh: 必需的；必不可少的；应得的
必需品；必要条件；要素

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁动词 requisit- 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「征用；申请单」
per-（彻底）+ 同根，义为「额外津贴；额外好处」
形容词加 -ly，义为「按要求地；必要地」

senses.title: Needed for a purpose
senses.definition: needed or necessary for a particular purpose or situation
senses.definitionCN: 为某个特定目的或情形所必需、不可缺少的
senses.example: Applicants must show the requisite language skills.
senses.exampleCN: 申请者必须展示必要的语言技能。
senses.why: The Latin source is requirere, to seek again or demand, so what is requisite is exactly what the task demands and cannot do without.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 requirere 意为「再次寻找、要求」，所以 requisite 指的正是任务索要、缺了就办不成的东西。

senses.title: A thing that is required
senses.definition: something that is needed, as a noun for a necessary object or condition
senses.definitionCN: 作为名词，指所必需的东西或条件
senses.example: The list of requisites for the camp includes boots and a lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 野营必需品清单上包括靴子和一盏灯。
senses.why: The same stack of demanded items becomes a concrete noun when the needed things are counted one by one.
senses.whyCN: 把清单上被要求的东西一件件点数，「必需」就从形容词变成可以清点的具体名词。

senses.title: Earned by right
senses.definition: deserved or due, used in formal and older prose
senses.definitionCN: 正式或较旧的说法，指应得的、理应获得的
senses.example: He received the requisite punishment for the offence.
senses.exampleCN: 他为这次过错受到了应得的惩罚。
senses.why: If something is demanded by a situation, it can also be owed to a person, and so the word slides into what is due.
senses.whyCN: 如果某种东西是情形所索要的，它也就可以「欠着」某个人，于是这个词滑向「应得」之意。

intro.en: Requisite comes through Old French from Latin requisitus, the past participle of requirere, to seek or demand again.
intro.cn: requisite 经古法语来自拉丁语 requisitus，即 requirere 的过去分词，意为「再次寻找、索求」。

items.en: Requirere means to seek again, need, or demand.
items.cn: requirere 意为再次寻找、需要、索求。

items.en: Requisitus is the past participle, meaning sought or required.
items.cn: requisitus 是过去分词，意为被寻求的、被要求的。

items.en: The learned adjective requisite enters French from the Latin participle.
items.cn: 文言的形容词 requisite 从拉丁分词进入法语。

items.en: Requisite first appears in English as a noun meaning a precondition.
items.cn: requisite 在英语中先作名词出现，指前提条件。

items.en: The adjective grows common in legal and administrative writing.
items.cn: 形容词用法在法律与行政文书里变得常见。

note.en: Requisite shares its root with requirement, require, and requisition, and sits near words for what is necessary.
note.cn: requisite 与 requirement、require、requisition 同根，并与一类表示「必需之物」的词相邻。

entries.definition: an official demand for something
entries.definitionCN: 正式征用；申请

entries.definition: something required before a start
entries.definitionCN: 前提条件；先修要求

entries.definition: an extra benefit attached to a job
entries.definitionCN: 额外津贴；额外好处

entries.definition: needed in order to be possible
entries.definitionCN: 必要的

entries.definition: absolutely necessary to the whole
entries.definitionCN: 必不可少的；本质的

entries.definition: cannot be done without
entries.definitionCN: 不可或缺的

normalIntro.en: Requisite is the demanded item on a list: what a task asks for before it can go ahead.
normalIntro.cn: requisite 是清单上被点名要的东西：任务开工之前必须先有的那一份。

normal.en: Requisite skills are the ones a job really needs.
normal.cn: requisite skills 指一份工作真正需要的技能。

normal.en: A requisite is a needed thing, the noun twin of requirement.
normal.cn: requisite 作名词时指必需之物，是 requirement 的名词兄弟。

normal.en: Add the prefix pre- and you get prerequisite, a condition required before starting.
normal.cn: 加前缀 pre- 就得到 prerequisite，指开始之前必须具备的条件。

normal.en: Add the suffix -ion and you get requisition, an official order for something.
normal.cn: 加后缀 -ion 就得到 requisition，指正式的征用或申请。

normal.en: Compare necessary and essential: requisite is more formal and often pairs with skills and qualifications.
normal.cn: 对比 necessary 与 essential：requisite 更正式，常与 skills、qualifications 搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a checklist where only one box is circled in red and marked as vital.
abstract.cn: 想象一张清单，只有一格被红笔圈住，旁边标着「非有不可」。

abstract.en: Think of a traveller packing only the few things without which the trip breaks.
abstract.cn: 想象一位旅人，只带上了少了几样行程就撑不下去的东西。

abstract.en: Imagine a scale that tips unless the due weight is placed on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆秤，不把应给的分量放上就压不平。

examples.en: The repairs were done without the requisite permit.
examples.cn: 这些修缮是在没有必需许可的情况下完成的。

examples.en: She has the requisite experience for the post.
examples.cn: 她具备这个职位所必需的经验。

examples.en: Books and warm clothes are the chief requisites of the trip.
examples.cn: 书本与保暖衣物是这趟旅程的主要必需品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞快威则特」——办事前先列一份「瑞」光闪闪的清单，缺哪样就办不成；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 requirere（再次寻找、索求）的过去分词 requisitus → 古法语 requisite → 英语 requisite，核心义「被索求、非有不可」。

sensesIntro.en: Requisite starts as a demanded condition, becomes the demanded object itself as a noun, and finally means what is due to someone.
sensesIntro.cn: requisite 首先指被索要的条件，作名词时指被要来的东西本身，最后还引申出「理应给某人的」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a checklist item circled in red and marked vital.
core.cn: 核心意象：清单上一项被红笔圈出，注明必须要有。

branches.en: What a task demands becomes the adjective needed for a purpose.
branches.cn: 任务所索求的东西变成「为某目的所必需」的形容词。

branches.en: Counting those demanded objects gives the noun sense of necessities.
branches.cn: 把被索要的东西逐一点数，就得到「必需品」的名词义。

branches.en: What a situation demands of someone can become what is owed to them.
branches.cn: 情形向人索要的东西，也可以转成应当给予他的东西。

branches.en: One requirement and one required item are the same demand at different levels.
branches.cn: 一条要求与一件必需品，是同一份需求在不同层次上的表现。

branches.en: Both a needed condition and a deserved outcome follow a demand with a claim to right.
branches.cn: 必需的条件与应得的结果，都跟着一份带正当性的索求。

intro.en: Requisite joins Latin re-, the intensive prefix, to quaerere, to seek, and it holds a whole word family.
intro.cn: requisite 由拉丁语前缀 re-（加强语气）加 quaerere（寻找）构成，并带出一整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin quaerere means to seek, and its compound requirere means to seek again or demand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quaerere 意为寻找，其复合形式 requirere 意为再次寻找或索求。

items.example: The prefix re- adds force to requirere.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 为 requirere 加上力度。

items.example: Quaerere supplies the image of searching.
items.exampleCN: quaerere 提供「寻找」的意象。

items.example: Requirere is the direct ancestor of the word.
items.exampleCN: requirere 是这个词的直接祖先。

items.example: Requisitus is the form borrowed as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: requisitus 是被借作形容词的形式。

items.example: Require is the everyday verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: require 是这个词族里最日常的动词。

items.example: Requirement adds the suffix -ment.
items.exampleCN: requirement 加上后缀 -ment。

items.meaningCN: 动作或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion builds requisition.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 requisition。

items.example: The prefix pre- builds prerequisite.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pre- 构成 prerequisite。

items.example: Inquisition shares the quaerere root.
items.exampleCN: inquisition 共享 quaerere 词根。

definition_zh: 征用；征购；申请单；要求
definition_en: an official order taking supplies or property for use, or a written request for something
core_image: 一张盖着公章的纸条，把仓库里的东西一件件点名搬走
scene: 军队行进途中物资不足，长官下令从附近仓库正式征用粮食和车辆。Short of supplies, the column issued a requisition for grain and lorries from the nearby depot.
sceneCN: 这里 requisition 是「征用」（第 1 个义项：以官方名义索要并取用物资）；句意：补给不足，这支队伍向附近仓库正式征用粮食与卡车。

pos.zh: 征用；征购；申请书；调拨单
征用；征购；申请领取

derivatives.zh: 由 requisition 加 -ist 构成，指负责办理申请或征用的人
同词族形容词，由拉丁分词直接借入，义为「必需的」
同根动词，义为「需要；要求」

senses.title: Official taking of supplies
senses.definition: the act of officially taking goods, property, or supplies for public or military use
senses.definitionCN: 以官方名义取用物资、财产或补给
senses.example: The army requisitioned several farms during the march.
senses.exampleCN: 行军途中军队征用了好几座农庄。
senses.why: The Latin noun requisitio names the act of seeking again and demanding, so requisition is the demand itself turned into an official act.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 requisitio 本指「一再索取」的动作，所以 requisition 就是那份索求被放大成的一项官方行为。

senses.title: A written request
senses.definition: a written or formal request for something that is needed
senses.definitionCN: 为需要的东西所写的书面或正式请求
senses.example: Please send a requisition for the new equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 请为这批新设备递一份申请单。
senses.why: The same demand often has to be written down, and the paper carrying it is also called a requisition.
senses.whyCN: 同样的索求常常要落在纸上，于是承载这份索求的那张纸也被叫作 requisition。

senses.title: A formal demand or claim
senses.definition: a formal claim or request made by a person or body in authority
senses.definitionCN: 由有权者正式提出的索取、要求
senses.example: Their requisition for more funds was rejected.
senses.exampleCN: 他们追加经费的要求被驳回了。
senses.why: Strip away the goods and what remains is plain demanding, so the word also serves for formal claims of any kind.
senses.whyCN: 把物资那一层去掉，剩下的是纯粹的「要」，于是这个词也用于任何正式的索取。

intro.en: Requisition comes from Latin requisitio, a seeking or demanding, from requirere, to seek again, through medieval French.
intro.cn: requisition 来自拉丁语 requisitio（寻求、索求），源于 requirere（再次寻找），再经中世纪法语进入英语。

items.en: Requirere means to seek again or demand.
items.cn: requirere 意为再次寻找或索求。

items.en: Requisitio names the act of seeking out or requesting.
items.cn: requisitio 指寻找或请求这一动作。

items.en: Requisition enters French law as a written demand.
items.cn: requisition 以书面索求之义进入法语法律用语。

items.en: English borrows the noun as a formal request, chiefly in law.
items.cn: 英语把这个名词借入，主要在法律中表示正式请求。

items.en: War and industry widen it to taking property and ordering supplies.
items.cn: 战争与工业使词义扩展到征用财产、订购物资。

note.en: Requisition belongs with the seeking family of requisite and require, and stands beside words for confiscation and request.
note.cn: requisition 属于 requisite、require 这条「寻求」词族，并与表示「没收、请求」的词相邻。

entries.definition: needed for a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 必需的；必需品

entries.definition: to need or demand
entries.definitionCN: 需要；要求

entries.definition: a person who requisitions goods
entries.definitionCN: 负责申请或征调物资的人

entries.definition: to take property officially as a penalty
entries.definitionCN: 没收；充公

entries.definition: to take hold of by force or law
entries.definitionCN: 夺取；扣押

entries.definition: the act of politely asking for
entries.definitionCN: 请求；要求

normalIntro.en: Requisition is the demand in paper form: the seeking of requisitio turned into an official act.
normalIntro.cn: requisition 是落在纸上的索求：requisitio 那种「一再索取」被变成一项官方行为。

normal.en: To requisition supplies is to take them officially for use.
normal.cn: requisition supplies 就是以官方名义取用物资。

normal.en: A requisition form is the sheet you fill in to ask for goods.
normal.cn: requisition form 就是申请领取东西时填的那张单子。

normal.en: The suffix -ion turns the Latin act noun into the English noun.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ion 把拉丁的动作名词变成英语名词。

normal.en: The family keeps the seeking meaning: require asks, requisite is needed, requisition takes.
normal.cn: 这个词族保留「找」的意思：require 是要求，requisite 是必需的，requisition 是取用。

normal.en: Compare confiscate: confiscation punishes, requisition supplies an urgent need.
normal.cn: 对比 confiscate：没收是惩罚，征用是满足急需。

abstract.en: Picture a soldier holding a stamped slip and walking out of a warehouse with sacks.
abstract.cn: 想象一名士兵举着盖了章的单子，扛着麻袋走出仓库。

abstract.en: Imagine a clerk typing a form, then the goods arriving at the door.
abstract.cn: 想象一名书记员打完一张表格，随后东西就送到了门口。

abstract.en: Think of a company asking head office for more money with a single sheet.
abstract.cn: 想象一家公司用一张纸上书总部，索取更多经费。

examples.en: The hospital requisitioned the building for extra beds.
examples.cn: 医院征用了这栋楼来增设床位。

examples.en: Fill in a requisition and the store will deliver the tools.
examples.cn: 填好调拨单，库房就会把这些工具送来。

examples.en: All requisitions for travel funds need a signature.
examples.cn: 所有差旅经费申请都需要签字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞快威齐神」——盖好章的单子一挥，仓库里的东西「齐」刷刷地搬走；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 requirere（再次寻找、索求）→ requisitio（寻求；索求）→ 中世纪法语 requisition → 英语 requisition，核心义「以官方名义索取、取用」。

sensesIntro.en: Requisition first means the official act of taking goods, then the written request that authorises it, and finally any formal claim.
sensesIntro.cn: requisition 先指官方取用物资的行为，再指授权这件事的书面申请，最后泛指任何正式索取。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamped slip that empties a warehouse.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张盖了章的单子把仓库搬空。

branches.en: The demanded goods are actually taken away in the military and public sense.
branches.cn: 军事与公共语境里，被索要的物资真的被搬走，就是「征用」。

branches.en: The demand written on paper becomes the form and the form becomes the word.
branches.cn: 写在纸上的索要成了表格，表格本身也成了这个词的意思。

branches.en: Without goods, the bare demand survives as any formal claim.
branches.cn: 不要物资，只剩纯粹的索取，就成了任何正式的要求。

branches.en: A paper requisition and the taking it authorises are one act seen twice.
branches.cn: 纸面申请与它授权的取用，是同一件事的两种看法。

branches.en: Both the form and the claim must come from someone with the right to ask.
branches.cn: 表格与索取都一样，必须出自有资格索取的人。

intro.en: Requisition is built on the Latin pair re- and quaerere, with -ion forming the act noun in English.
intro.cn: requisition 建于拉丁语 re- 与 quaerere 这一对成分之上，英语用 -ion 构成动作名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin requirere, to seek again, supplies requisitio, the act of seeking or demanding.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 requirere（再次寻找）提供了 requisitio，意为寻求或索求的动作。

items.example: The prefix re- strengthens requirere.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 加强了 requirere 的语气。

items.example: Quaerere is the verb at the heart of the family.
items.exampleCN: quaerere 是这个词族的核心动词。

items.example: Requirere yields the participle requisitus.
items.exampleCN: requirere 产出分词 requisitus。

items.example: Requisitio is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: requisitio 是直接的拉丁来源。

items.meaningCN: 动作或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -tion keeps the act sense.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tion 保留了动作含义。

items.example: Requisite is the young sibling in the family.
items.exampleCN: requisite 是词族里较年轻的成员。

items.example: Require is the plain English verb.
items.exampleCN: require 是最朴素的英语动词。

items.example: Conquistador shares the quaerere root by a long road.
items.exampleCN: conquistador 绕了远路也共享 quaerere 词根。

items.example: Exquisite comes from exquirere, to seek out.
items.exampleCN: exquisite 来自 exquirere，意为搜求出来。

definition_zh: 怨恨；愤愤不平；对……不满
definition_en: to feel angry or bitter about something, usually because it seems unfair
core_image: 一个人被推了一把，脸上没出声，心里却把那一下反复重嚼
scene: 弟弟被安排多做家务，表面答应，心里却越想越气，觉得这条规矩不公平。Asked to do extra chores, the brother agreed aloud but began to resent the unfair rule.
sceneCN: 这里 resent 是「怨恨、愤愤不平」（第 1 个义项：因觉得不公而对某事心生怨气）；句意：被要求多做家务，弟弟嘴上答应，心里却开始怨恨这条不公平的规矩。

pos.zh: 怨恨；愤恨；对……感到不满

derivatives.zh: resent 加名词后缀 -ment，义为「怨恨；愤懑」
resent 加形容词后缀 -ful，义为「满怀怨恨的」
resentful 加 -ly，义为「愤愤地」

senses.title: Bitter anger at unfairness
senses.definition: to feel anger or bitterness about something that seems unfair or unjust
senses.definitionCN: 对看似不公或不义的事感到愤怒与苦涩
senses.example: She resented the way the decision was made.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这个决定的做法心怀怨恨。
senses.why: The Old French source means to feel strongly, and the sense narrowed to strong feeling about wrong, so resent is the heart that keeps chewing an unfairness.
senses.whyCN: 古法语来源意为「强烈感受」，后收窄为对不公的强烈感受，所以 resent 是那颗反复咀嚼不平的心。

senses.title: Objection to an intrusion
senses.definition: to dislike or object to something as unwelcome or intrusive
senses.definitionCN: 把某事视为多余打扰而讨厌或反对
senses.example: The staff resent being watched while they work.
senses.exampleCN: 员工们反感工作时被监视。
senses.why: Anything that pushes into a person without asking feels like a slight, so resent widens from unfair wrongs to mere intrusion.
senses.whyCN: 任何不经允许便闯进一个人生活的事都像一次冒犯，于是 resent 从不公之屈扩展到单纯的打扰。

senses.title: To feel again
senses.definition: to feel again, a rare and old sense echoing the literal prefix
senses.definitionCN: 罕用且古老的义项，照着字面前缀意为「再感受一次」
senses.example: The old poets used resent for feeling a thing once more.
senses.exampleCN: 古代诗人用 resent 表示把某种感受再体会一遍。
senses.why: The prefix re- means again and the verb means to feel, so taken literally the word once meant to feel a second time.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 re- 意为再次，动词意为感受，若照字面拆，这个词曾经就表示「再一次感受」。

intro.en: Resent comes from French ressentir, a compound of Latin re-, again, and sentire, to feel, with a rare older sense of feeling again.
intro.cn: resent 来自法语 ressentir，由拉丁语 re-（再次）与 sentire（感受）复合而成，早期还有罕用的「再次感受」之义。

items.en: Sentire means to feel or perceive.
items.cn: sentire 意为感受、察觉。

items.en: The prefix re- adds the idea of again.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 加上「再次」的意思。

items.en: Ressentir means to feel something keenly or in return.
items.cn: ressentir 意为强烈地感受或回报地感受。

items.en: Resent enters English first in the sense of feeling a thing again.
items.cn: resent 进入英语时先表示「再度感受某物」。

items.en: The sense narrows to take ill, to be angry at an injury.
items.cn: 词义收窄为「为受到的伤害而不平、恼怒」。

items.en: The literal feeling again sense becomes rare.
items.cn: 字面的「再次感受」义变得罕用。

note.en: Resent is not the past of resend; it belongs to the Latin feeling family of sense, sentiment, and sensible.
note.cn: resent 不是 resend 的过去式；它属于 sense、sentiment、sensible 这条「感觉」词族。

entries.definition: bitter anger at unfair treatment
entries.definitionCN: 怨恨；愤懑

entries.definition: full of bitterness
entries.definitionCN: 满怀怨恨的

entries.definition: to send again; only looks alike, a different word
entries.definitionCN: 重新发送；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to feel annoyed that someone has something
entries.definitionCN: 妒忌；不情愿给予

entries.definition: a lasting feeling of resentment
entries.definitionCN: 积怨；怨恨

entries.definition: to not like something
entries.definitionCN: 不喜欢

normalIntro.en: Resent is feeling something again and again: the heart keeps returning to a hurt that seems unfair.
normalIntro.cn: resent 是把某种感受一次次重新体验：心不断回到那处让人觉得不公的伤口。

normal.en: Resent is a verb, not the past of resend, so write I resent it rather than I resent the email.
normal.cn: resent 是动词本身，不是 resend 的过去式，所以要说「我对此不满」，而不是「我重发了邮件」。

normal.en: Add the suffix -ment and you get the noun resentment.
normal.cn: 加后缀 -ment 就得到名词 resentment。

normal.en: Add the suffix -ful and you get the adjective resentful.
normal.cn: 加后缀 -ful 就得到形容词 resentful。

normal.en: Resent takes what or that: she resents being left out.
normal.cn: resent 常接动名词或 that 从句：她因被排除在外而不满。

normal.en: Share the sentire root with sense, sentiment, and sensitive.
normal.cn: 与 sense、sentiment、sensitive 共享 sentire（感受）词根。

abstract.en: Picture a person chewing a small injustice again and again without speaking.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人默不作声，把一桩小小的不公反复咀嚼。

abstract.en: Think of a guest whose chair is pushed too close and who keeps inching away.
abstract.cn: 想象一位客人被人把椅子推得太近，于是一点点往外挪。

abstract.en: Imagine listening to the same song a second time and feeling it anew.
abstract.cn: 想象把同一首歌再听一遍，重新体会那阵情绪。

examples.en: Many workers resent the long hours imposed on them.
examples.cn: 许多工人对被强加的长工时心怀怨恨。

examples.en: He resented being asked to explain every decision.
examples.cn: 他反感每做一个决定都要解释。

examples.en: The villagers resent the new road through the old orchard.
examples.cn: 村民们对穿过老果园的新路很反感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞怎特」——心里越想越「怎」么这么「特」别不公平，一股气就上来了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sentire（感受）加前缀 re-（再次）→ 古法语 ressentir（强烈感受）→ 英语 resent，核心义「把不公的感受一再体会」。

sensesIntro.en: Resent begins as feeling again, hardens into bitterness at unfairness, and slackens into objection to any intrusion.
sensesIntro.cn: resent 由「再次感受」起步，硬化为对不公的怨恨，又松化为对任何打扰的反感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heart that keeps chewing on one unfair push.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗心反复咀嚼那一下不公的推搡。

branches.en: Feeling again deepens into bitterness at what seems unjust.
branches.cn: 反复感受便加深为对看似不义之事的心怀怨恨。

branches.en: The same soreness applies to any unwelcome intrusion.
branches.cn: 同样的刺痛也适用于任何不受欢迎的闯入。

branches.en: The literal sense of feeling a second time survives only in older texts.
branches.cn: 字面的「再一次感受」只残存在较旧的文本里。

branches.en: A grudge and a dislike of intrusion both start when a boundary is crossed.
branches.cn: 积怨与对打扰的反感，都起于边界被越过。

branches.en: The repeated feeling of a past hurt feeds present resentment.
branches.cn: 对旧伤的反复回想，喂养着当下的怨恨。

intro.en: Resent carries the Latin re- of again and the sentire of feeling, with -ment and -ful building the family.
intro.cn: resent 带着拉丁语 re-（再次）与 sentire（感受），再由 -ment、-ful 等词尾撑起整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire means to feel, and with the prefix re- it becomes feeling something again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sentire 意为感受，加上前缀 re- 便成为「再次感受某物」。

items.example: The prefix re- gives resent its original sense of feeling again.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 赋予 resent 原本「再次感受」的意思。

items.example: Sentire is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: sentire 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: Ressentir is the French form English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: ressentir 是英语借入的法语形式。

items.meaningCN: 状态或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ment builds resentment.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ment 构成 resentment。

items.example: The suffix -ful builds resentful.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ful 构成 resentful。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns resentful into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 把 resentful 变成副词。

items.example: Sense shares the sentire root.
items.exampleCN: sense 共享 sentire 词根。

items.example: Sentiment keeps the feeling sense plainly.
items.exampleCN: sentiment 明显保留了感受之义。

items.example: Sensitive is another child of sentire.
items.exampleCN: sensitive 也是 sentire 的后代。

definition_zh: 居留权；居住期限；驻地工作期；住院医师培训期；驻场创作；住所
definition_en: the official right to live in a country, or a period spent living and working in a particular place
core_image: 一张盖了章的许可纸，旁边是某人在异乡落脚的房门
scene: 机场的入境窗口前排着长队，一位留学生把刚拿到的居留许可递进窗口。After three years of study, she finally obtained permanent residency in the country.
sceneCN: 这里 residency 是「居留权」（第 1 个义项：在某国长期合法居住的正式权利）；句意：学成三年之后，她终于获得了该国的永久居留权。

pos.zh: 居留权；居住期限；驻地工作期；住院医师培训期；驻场创作期

derivatives.zh: 基础词 resid- 加 -ent 构成，义为「居民；住院医师」
由 residential 词干加 -ial 构成，义为「住宅的；住宿的」
基础动词，义为「居住；定居」
加否定前缀 non- 构成，义为「非居民的」

senses.title: The right to live in a country
senses.definition: the legal right of a person to live in a particular country for a long or permanent period
senses.definitionCN: 某人在特定国家长期或永久居住的合法权利
senses.example: The graduate applied for residency after finding a job in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这名毕业生在城里找到工作后申请了居留权。
senses.why: The Latin stem residere means to remain sitting in a place, so residency is the official state of being allowed to stay.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词干 residere 意为「坐在某处不走」，所以 residency 就是被正式允许留下来的状态。

senses.title: A period of official residence
senses.definition: the length of time during which someone formally resides in a place, often fixed by a rule
senses.definitionCN: 某人正式在某地居住的时间长度，常由规定限定
senses.example: Tax rules may require a minimum residency of one hundred and eighty days.
senses.exampleCN: 税务规则可能要求至少一百八十天的居留期。
senses.why: The suffix -cy names a state, and a state can be measured in time, so residency also means the span of staying.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -cy 表示状态，而状态可以按时间计量，所以 residency 也指居住的时长。

senses.title: A training post in a hospital
senses.definition: a period of supervised practical training that a doctor completes at a hospital after graduating
senses.definitionCN: 医生毕业后在医院接受指导性临床训练的时期
senses.example: He finished his residency in pediatrics last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他去年春天完成了儿科住院医师培训。
senses.why: A young doctor lives at the hospital for a few years, keeping the older sense of staying in a place.
senses.whyCN: 年轻医生要在医院里生活工作好几年，保留了「在某处停留」的老意思。

senses.title: A stay in a workplace
senses.definition: a fixed period during which a journalist, diplomat, or musician works in one place as part of a job
senses.definitionCN: 记者、外交官或音乐家因公在某一地点工作的一段固定时间
senses.example: Her three-year residency with the orchestra ended in June.
senses.exampleCN: 她在这个乐团的三年驻地工作于六月结束。
senses.why: Stay plus duty: the job places a person somewhere for a term, and that term is called a residency.
senses.whyCN: 「停留」加上「职责」：工作把人安置在某个地方一段时间，这段时间就叫 residency。

senses.title: A creative placement
senses.definition: a period during which an artist or writer is invited to live and work at a school, studio, or other institution
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家或作家受邀在院校、工作室或其他机构生活与创作的时期
senses.example: The gallery offers a six-month residency to young painters.
senses.exampleCN: 这家画廊为年轻画家提供为期六个月的驻场创作期。
senses.why: The institution keeps the artist inside it for a while, so the word moves from legal staying to creative living.
senses.whyCN: 机构把艺术家接纳在自己内部一段时间，这个词就从法律上的居留延伸到创作上的驻场。

senses.title: A place where one lives
senses.definition: a formal word for a place of living, usually alongside the words place of
senses.definitionCN: 对居住地的正式说法，通常与 place of 连用
senses.example: Please state your place of residency on the form.
senses.exampleCN: 请在表格上注明你的居住地。
senses.why: If residency can be a state of staying, the place it happens in can take the same name in formal usage.
senses.whyCN: 既然 residency 可以指停留的状态，那么在正式用法里，发生这种停留的地方也能用同一个词来称呼。

intro.en: Residency is the Latin stem residere plus the noun suffix -cy, and it joined English through the older word resident.
intro.cn: residency 是拉丁语词干 residere 加名词后缀 -cy，经由更早的 resident 进入英语。

items.en: Sedere means to sit, and the prefix re- means back; residere means to remain sitting behind, that is to stay.
items.cn: sedere 意为「坐」，前缀 re- 表示「向后」；residere 意为「坐在原处不退」，即「留下」。

items.en: Residentia, from residere, means a staying behind or a dwelling place.
items.cn: 由 residere 派生的 residentia 意为「留下、居所」。

items.en: Resident and residence reach English from Latin through Old French forms such as resident and residence.
items.cn: resident 与 residence 经古法语形式（如 resident、residence）从拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: Resident is recorded in Middle English; residency appears later as the state noun. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: resident 在中古英语中已有记录；residency 作为状态名词出现得更晚。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Official language uses residency for the right and the period of staying in a country.
items.cn: 官方用语用 residency 指在某国居留的权利与期限。

items.en: Medicine and the arts borrow the word for a staying: a hospital training post and an artist placement.
items.cn: 医学与艺术界借用了「停留」的意思：住院医师培训期与艺术家驻场。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other words of the same staying family; the near-meaning group gathers other words for rights to stay and lengths of stay.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「停留」词族的其他词；近义组收其他表示居留权利与居住期限的词。

entries.definition: to live in a particular place
entries.definitionCN: 在某地居住

entries.definition: a person who lives in a place
entries.definitionCN: 在同一词根上构成的词，义为「居民」

entries.definition: a house where someone lives, or the act of living there
entries.definitionCN: 同族名词，义为「住宅；居住」，与 residency 常被混用，注意结尾 -ence 与 -ency 的区别

entries.definition: the legal position of being a member of a state, stronger than residency
entries.definitionCN: 国籍、公民身份，法律地位强于居留权

entries.definition: an official document allowing someone to do something
entries.definitionCN: 许可证；准照，居留权通常以许可证的形式体现

entries.definition: the right to hold a post or property for a period
entries.definitionCN: 任职期或持有期，侧重职位而非居留

normalIntro.en: Residency is the state of remaining in a place, so the words resident and reside are its best hooks.
normalIntro.cn: residency 是「留在某处」的状态，所以 resident 与 reside 是最好的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Residency shares its stem with resident: a resident is the person, residency is the right or the term.
normal.cn: residency 与 resident 同词干：resident 是人，residency 是权利或期限。

normal.en: Permanent residency is the right to stay for good.
normal.cn: permanent residency 是长期留下来的权利。

normal.en: Attention to spelling: advice, residence, and residency all carry -cy for the state.
normal.cn: 注意拼写：表示状态的名词常以 -cy 结尾，如 residency。

normal.en: A medical residency is years of staying at a hospital as a trainee.
normal.cn: medical residency 是作为受训医生在医院待上好几年。

normal.en: Reside, resident, residence, residency: one Latin verb, one idea of staying put.
normal.cn: reside、resident、residence、residency：一个拉丁动词，一个「留下来」的意思。

abstract.en: Imagine a rubber stamp coming down hard on a paper: the stamp is the legal right to stay.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章重重盖在纸上：这枚章就是留下来的法律权利。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with a long line of days crossing a border; that line is the residency period.
abstract.cn: 想象一本日历上有一条长长的日子横跨边境线：那条线就是居留期限。

abstract.en: See a young doctor walking the same hospital corridor at dawn, month after month; that staying is the training.
abstract.cn: 想象年轻医生月复一月在拂晓走过同一条医院走廊：这份停留就是培训期。

examples.en: She was granted permanent residency after five years of work.
examples.cn: 工作五年后，她获得了永久居留权。

examples.en: The visa is only valid during the student residency.
examples.cn: 这张签证仅在学生居留期间有效。

examples.en: The sculptor spent a year in an artist residency in Berlin.
examples.cn: 这位雕塑家在柏林参加了一年的驻场创作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞记登西」——瑞记的地址登记在西方：拿到了居留权。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 residere（留下；坐住）= re-（向后）+ sedere（坐），派生 residentia（停留、居所）；古法语传入英语成为 resident/residence，再加后缀 -cy 构成 residency，核心义「留在某处」。

sensesIntro.en: Residency begins as the official state of staying in a country, then turns into the measured period of staying, and then spreads to placements where people stay to work, train, or create.
sensesIntro.cn: residency 先指在某国居留的正式状态，再指可以计算的居住期限，随后扩展到人们为了工作、受训或创作而停留在某处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person stays put in a new country, and a stamped paper says the stay is allowed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人在新国家留下来不走，一张盖章的纸说明这份停留被允许。

branches.en: The right to stay in a country is the legal sense, the most common one today.
branches.cn: 在某国居留的权利是法律义项，也是今天最常用的意思。

branches.en: Once staying is allowed, it can be counted in days and years.
branches.cn: 一旦停留被许可，它就可以按天、按年计算。

branches.en: A hospital training post keeps the staying idea inside medicine.
branches.cn: 医院里的培训岗位把「停留」的意思留在医学领域。

branches.en: A stay in a workplace turns the right into a duty with a fixed term.
branches.cn: 在工作地点的一段停留，把权利变成了有固定期限的职责。

branches.en: Creative placements and places of living are the two ends: a stay for art, and the address of a stay.
branches.cn: 驻场创作与居住地是两端：一个为创作而停留，一个记录停留的地址。

intro.en: Residency is built from the Latin prefix re-, the Latin root sedere, and the English noun suffix -cy.
intro.cn: residency 由拉丁语前缀 re-、拉丁词根 sedere 与英语名词后缀 -cy 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin sedere means to sit; with re- it becomes residere, to stay behind, and its noun residentia gives the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sedere 意为「坐」；加 re- 后成为 residere「留在后面」，其名词 residentia 给出英语词族。

items.example: The prefix points to staying behind rather than leaving.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀指留下而不是离开。

items.example: To sit still is the picture behind staying.
items.exampleCN: 坐着不动就是「停留」背后的画面。

items.example: Residere joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: residere 把前缀与词根合在一起。

items.example: This noun feeds the English residence.
items.exampleCN: 这个词给英语的 residence 提供了来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示「人」或「处于某种状态」
items.example: It forms resident.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 resident。

items.example: It forms residence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 residence。

items.example: It forms residency from the base of resident.
items.exampleCN: 它由 resident 的词干构成 residency。

items.example: It forms residential.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 residential。

items.example: It forms nonresident.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 nonresident。

definition_zh: 残余物；渣滓；残留物；（法律）剩余遗产
definition_en: the part that is left over after the main part has gone or has been used
core_image: 滤网底下剩下的那层渣子，主体已经流走了
scene: 实验室的漏斗里，咖啡液滴尽了，滤纸上留下一圈深褐色的残渣。A dark residue of coffee grounds was left at the bottom of the filter.
sceneCN: 这里 residue 是「残余物；残留物」（第 1 个义项：主体被取走或滤走之后剩下的部分）；句意：滤纸底部留下了一圈深褐色的咖啡渣。

pos.zh: 残余物；渣滓；残留物；剩余遗产

derivatives.zh: 本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「残留的；剩余的」
直接借自拉丁语的中性形式，义为「残余物；剩余物」
residue 加 -ary 构成，义为「剩余遗产的」

senses.title: Something left after removal
senses.definition: a small amount of something that remains after the main part has been removed, used up, or processed
senses.definitionCN: 主体被移走、用尽或加工后剩下的少量物质
senses.example: Wash the cup carefully to remove any residue of soap.
senses.exampleCN: 仔细清洗杯子，去掉残留的肥皂。
senses.why: Latin residuum meant what is left behind, and the same image of a leftover part runs through every sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 residuum 意为「留下来的东西」，「剩下的那部分」这个意象贯穿所有义项。

senses.title: Traces left by a process
senses.definition: traces of a substance that a process leaves on a surface or in a product
senses.definitionCN: 某过程在表面或产品上留下的物质痕迹
senses.example: Scientists tested the vegetables for pesticide residue.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家检测了蔬菜中的农药残留。
senses.why: When an action finishes, its material trace stays on the object, and that trace is called the residue.
senses.whyCN: 一个过程结束后，它的物质痕迹会留在物体上，这个痕迹就被称为 residue。

senses.title: The rest after division in maths
senses.definition: the amount left when one number cannot be exactly divided by another
senses.definitionCN: 一个数不能被另一个数整除时剩下的量
senses.example: Nine divided by two leaves a residue of one.
senses.exampleCN: 九除以二，余数是一。
senses.why: Division takes whole groups away and stops; whatever could not be taken is literally the remainder.
senses.whyCN: 除法是整组整组地取走然后停下，没能取走的那一点，字面上就是「剩下的东西」。

senses.title: Scientific leftovers of decay
senses.titleCN: （生物学、化学的）残基；加工副产物
senses.definition: material left after a substance has broken down or an organism has decomposed, as studied in chemistry or biology
senses.definitionCN: 物质分解或生物体腐烂之后留下的物质，是化学与生物学的研究对象
senses.example: Corn stalks and other crop residue can be turned into fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 玉米秸秆和其他作物残料可以转化为燃料。
senses.why: In the laboratory the leftover is priced and named: what refuses to vanish is the residue of the reaction.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室里，剩下的东西会被计量并命名：不肯消失的那部分就是反应的残留物。

senses.title: What remains of an estate
senses.definition: the part of the money and property of a dead person that is left after all debts, taxes, and specific gifts are paid
senses.definitionCN: 偿还债务、缴纳税款并分配特定遗赠之后剩下的那部分遗产
senses.example: The widow inherited the residue of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 遗孀继承了剩余的遗产。
senses.why: Law takes the same arithmetic ordering: pay what is owed first, and whatever is left is the residue.
senses.whyCN: 法律沿用同样的清算顺序：先清偿所欠，剩下的那部分就是 residue。

senses.title: A figurative remainder
senses.definition: a small amount of a feeling, fact, or influence that continues after its main cause has ended
senses.definitionCN: 在其主要起因消失之后仍然持续的一点点感觉、事实或影响
senses.example: There was a residue of anger in her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她的声音里还留有余怒。
senses.why: Feelings and events also leave sediment: when the event is over, a faint trace of it may still remain.
senses.whyCN: 情绪与事件也会留下沉淀：事情过去了，它的一点淡淡痕迹仍可能留着。

intro.en: Residue comes from Old French residu, from the Latin adjective residuus and the noun residuum, both built on residere.
intro.cn: residue 来自古法语 residu，源于拉丁语形容词 residuus 与名词 residuum，二者都由 residere 构成。

items.en: Sedere means to sit; with re- it forms residere, to remain sitting, that is to stay back.
items.cn: sedere 意为「坐」；加 re- 构成 residere，意为「坐在原处、留了下来」。

items.en: From residere come the adjective residuus, remaining, and the neuter noun residuum, what is left behind.
items.cn: 由 residere 派生出形容词 residuus（剩余的）与中性名词 residuum（剩下的东西）。

items.en: Old French residu carries the noun into English, keeping the idea of what is left over.
items.cn: 古法语 residu 把这个名词带入英语，保留「剩下的东西」之意。

items.en: Residue is recorded in Middle English; the related Latin form residuum is also borrowed later as a learned word.
items.cn: residue 在中古英语中已有记录；相关的拉丁形式 residuum 也在后世作为书面词被借入。

items.en: Science and law each adopt the word: a chemical left in a sample, and what remains of an estate.
items.cn: 科学与法律各自采用这个词：样品中的化学残留，以及遗产的剩余部分。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other members of the Latin remaining family; the near-meaning group gathers words for what is left over or what is added back.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「留下」词族的其他成员；近义组收表示「剩下的东西」以及与「剩余」相对的词。

entries.definition: to live in a particular place
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的动词，义为「居住、停留」

entries.definition: remaining after the main part has gone
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加后缀构成的形容词，义为「残留的、剩余的」

entries.definition: a person who lives in a place
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，义为「居民」，强调「留在某处的人」

entries.definition: solid material that settles at the bottom of a liquid
entries.definitionCN: 沉淀在液体底部的固体物，特指沉下去的东西

entries.definition: food or material not used up, informal in tone
entries.definitionCN: 没吃完或没用完的剩余物，语气日常，常指剩饭

entries.definition: the part of something that is still there when the rest is gone
entries.definitionCN: 其余部分，强调与「已处理部分」相对的剩余，不一定是渣滓

normalIntro.en: Residue belongs to the Latin family of sedere, to sit, so its hooks come from that sit-still root.
normalIntro.cn: residue 属于拉丁语 sedere（坐）的词族，记忆钩子都来自这个「坐着不走」的词根。

normal.en: The r-e-s of residue repeats in reside, resident, and residual; all are about staying.
normal.cn: residue 开头的同一串字母在 reside、resident、residual 中反复出现，都与「留下」有关。

normal.en: Sediment is the sediment of a liquid, while residue is what any process leaves behind.
normal.cn: sediment 特指液体中的沉淀，而 residue 泛指任何过程剩下的东西。

normal.en: Pesticide residue is what testing finds on fruit, so the word often appears in food safety news.
normal.cn: pesticide residue 是检测在水果上发现的残留，这个词常出现在食品安全新闻里。

normal.en: In law and in arithmetic, residue is the amount left after everything owed has been taken.
normal.cn: 在法律与算术中，residue 都是把该扣的扣完之后剩下的数量。

normal.en: Leave a residue means to leave a mark that is hard to remove.
normal.cn: leave a residue 意为留下难以清除的痕迹。

abstract.en: Picture a coffee filter: the liquid has gone, and a ring of grounds is all that stays.
abstract.cn: 想象一只咖啡滤纸：液体流走了，只剩下一圈咖啡渣。

abstract.en: Imagine your fingers after wiping a dusty table: a grey film on them is the residue.
abstract.cn: 想象擦完落满灰尘的桌子后的手指：上面那层灰就是残留物。

abstract.en: Think of a division sum that cannot finish: the small number left on the paper is the remainder.
abstract.cn: 想一想一道除不尽的算式：纸上剩下的小数就是余数。

examples.en: The factory was ordered to clean up the chemical residue in the river.
examples.cn: 这家工厂被勒令清理河中的化学残留物。

examples.en: A thin residue of salt was left on the windscreen.
examples.cn: 挡风玻璃上留下了一层薄薄的盐迹。

examples.en: After the debts were paid, the residue of the estate went to his sister.
examples.cn: 债务清偿后，剩余遗产归了他的姐姐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞记丢」——瑞记的东西都丢光了，只剩一点残余。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 residere（留下；坐住）= re-（向后）+ sedere（坐）；派生形容词 residuus 与名词 residuum，经古法语 residu 进入英语成为 residue，核心义「留在原处的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: Residue starts from the physical leftover and spreads to chemical traces, mathematical remainders, legal estates, and faint remains of feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: residue 从实体残留出发，扩展到化学痕迹、数学余数、法律遗产以及情感的淡痕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the main stream has passed, and a layer of dregs lies at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：主流已经过去，底下还躺着一层渣子。

branches.en: A physical leftover and the traces a process leaves are the concrete senses.
branches.cn: 实体残留与过程留下的痕迹是最具体的义项。

branches.en: Arithmetic counts the leftover when division cannot finish cleanly.
branches.cn: 算术在不能整除时计量剩下的那一点。

branches.en: Chemistry and biology name what survives decay and processing.
branches.cn: 化学与生物学用这个词命名经受分解与加工后仍留存的部分。

branches.en: Law pays debts first, and the remaining share is the residue.
branches.cn: 法律先清偿债务，剩下的那一份就是剩余遗产。

branches.en: The faint trace of a feeling is the concrete residue moved into the mind.
branches.cn: 情绪的淡淡痕迹，就是实体残留被移到了心里。

intro.en: Residue is built from the Latin prefix re- and the Latin root sedere, with English suffixes growing the family.
intro.cn: residue 由拉丁语前缀 re- 与拉丁词根 sedere 构成，英语后缀再扩展出这个家族。

latinIntro.en: Latin residere, residuus, and residuum all come from sedere, to sit, and re-, back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 residere、residuus 与 residuum 都来自 sedere（坐）与 re-（向后）。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of staying behind the others.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加上「躲在别人后面」的意思。

items.example: Sitting and not leaving is the core picture.
items.exampleCN: 坐着不走就是核心画面。

items.example: The verb gives the family its staying idea.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给词族带来「停留」的意思。

items.example: The adjective turns the verb into a description of what is left.
items.exampleCN: 形容词把动词转为对「剩下之物」的描述。

items.example: The Latin noun is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: It forms residual.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 residual。

items.example: It forms residuary in legal language.
items.exampleCN: 在法律用语中它构成 residuary。

items.meaning: matter that settles at the bottom
items.example: Sediment shares the sitting root, but names only what sinks.
items.exampleCN: sediment 共享「坐」这个词根，但只指沉下去的东西。

definition_zh: （声音）回响；产生共鸣；引起共鸣；共振
definition_en: to produce a deep, full sound that continues for a while, or to connect strongly with feelings or ideas
core_image: 敲一下音叉，声音在两个相似的物体之间来回弹跳、越来越亮
scene: 讲者说到母亲在车站送别的一段往事，台下许多人都安静下来。Her words resonated with the audience because every listener had known that farewell.
sceneCN: 这里 resonate 是「引起共鸣」（第 3 个义项：话语与听者的感受产生强烈呼应）；句意：她的话引起了听众的共鸣，因为每位听众都经历过那样的离别。

pos.zh: 回响；产生共鸣；引起共鸣；共振

derivatives.zh: 本词加名词后缀构成，义为「共鸣；共振；洪亮」
本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「洪亮的；引起共鸣的」
resonate 加 -or 构成，义为「共鸣器；谐振器」
在 resonant 后加 -ly 构成，义为「洪亮地；引起共鸣地」

senses.title: To ring and continue sounding
senses.definition: of a sound, to be loud, deep, and to continue for some time after it is made
senses.definitionCN: 声音响亮低沉，在发出之后仍持续一段时间
senses.example: The bell resonated across the valley for a full minute.
senses.exampleCN: 钟声在山谷里回荡了整整一分钟。
senses.why: Latin sonare means to sound, and re- adds back, so resonate is sound coming back after the strike.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sonare 意为「发声」，re- 表示「回」，所以 resonate 是敲击之后折返回来的声音。

senses.title: To vibrate in sympathy
senses.definition: of an object or space, to vibrate strongly when it is hit by a sound of a matching natural frequency
senses.definitionCN: 物体或空间被与其固有频率相配的声音击中时强烈振动
senses.example: The glass resonated when the singer reached the same pitch.
senses.exampleCN: 当歌手唱到同一音高时，玻璃杯随之共振。
senses.why: Physics took the ringing image and gave it a cause: another wave of the same frequency pushes the object to answer it.
senses.whyCN: 物理学借用「回响」的画面并给出原因：另一个频率相同的波推动物体作出回应。

senses.title: To connect with someone
senses.definition: of words, ideas, or events, to produce a strong emotional response in someone because they seem personally true
senses.definitionCN: 话语、想法或事件让人深有感触，因为听起来与自己的经历真实贴合
senses.example: His story of leaving home resonated with many young readers.
senses.exampleCN: 他离家求学的故事引起了许多年轻读者的共鸣。
senses.why: The listening ear is treated like a body that vibrates: matching feelings are struck and answer back.
senses.whyCN: 聆听的耳朵被当作会振动的物体：相符的情感被敲响，于是反过来回应。

senses.title: To have meaning or importance
senses.titleCN: 具有重要意义；意义深远
senses.definition: to be important or meaningful to someone, especially in a historical or personal setting
senses.definitionCN: 对某人具有重要意义，尤用于历史或个人语境
senses.example: The old photograph resonates more strongly now than it did then.
senses.exampleCN: 这张老照片如今的意义比当年更深远。
senses.why: Something meaningful keeps returning to mind, as a sound keeps returning to the ear.
senses.whyCN: 有意义的东西会一次次回到心里，正如声音会一次次回到耳朵里。

senses.title: To fill a place with sound
senses.definition: of a voice or sound, to fill a building or space and be heard long and clearly
senses.definitionCN: 声音或嗓音充满某座建筑或空间，并被长久清晰地听见
senses.example: The organ resonated through the cathedral during the service.
senses.exampleCN: 礼拜时管风琴的声音响彻大教堂。
senses.why: Sound that bounces off walls lasts longer, so a space with hard walls seems to magnify the echo.
senses.whyCN: 撞上墙壁后反弹的声音持续更久，所以硬墙面的空间会显得把回声放大。

senses.title: To fit together in harmony
senses.definition: to be closely related to or consistent with something else, so the two seem to belong together
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物关系紧密或相互一致，仿佛本该相伴
senses.example: Her designs resonate with the traditions of the region.
senses.exampleCN: 她的设计与该地区的传统相呼应。
senses.why: Two things that agree are like two strings tuned alike: strike one and the other is set moving.
senses.whyCN: 相互契合的两个事物如同调好的两根弦：拨动其一，另一根也随之而动。

intro.en: Resonate comes from the Latin verb resonare, to sound again, built from the prefix re- and the verb sonare, to sound.
intro.cn: resonate 来自拉丁语动词 resonare（再次发声），由前缀 re- 与动词 sonare（发声）构成。

items.en: Sonare means to sound or make a noise, and sonus is a sound.
items.cn: sonare 意为「发声、发出声响」，名词 sonus 意为「声音」。

items.en: The prefix re-, back or again, is added to sonare: resonare means to resound or echo back.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 表示「回、再」，加在 sonare 前面：resonare 意为「回响、发出回声」。

items.en: The participle resonans and the noun resonantia describe echoing sound.
items.cn: 分词 resonans 与名词 resonantia 都用来描写回荡的声音。

items.en: Scientific Latin uses resonantia for the vibration of bodies that sound in sympathy, a meaning that passes into modern physics.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语用 resonantia 指物体之间相互应和而产生的振动，这一含义后来进入现代物理学。

items.en: French résonner and the English noun resonance carry the word into English; the verb resonate is recorded from the nineteenth century. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 法语 résonner 与英语名词 resonance 把这个词带入英语；动词 resonate 可见于十九世纪。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Modern English extends the word from sound to feelings and ideas that strike a matching chord.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词从声音扩展到拨动相似心弦的情感与想法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the sound family built on Latin sonare; the near-meaning group gathers sounds that carry, and feelings that connect.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语 sonare（声音）之上的词族；近义组收表示声音回荡与情感呼应的词。

entries.definition: the quality of a sound being deep and continuing, or of a vibration echoing back
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加后缀构成的名词，义为「共鸣、共振、洪亮」

entries.definition: of a sound, deep and continuing; of a place, full of echoing sound
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「洪亮的、充满回声的」，也指「引起共鸣的」

entries.definition: a system that finds objects under water by sending out sound
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，义为「声呐」，用声音探测水下物体

entries.definition: a sound that comes back after bouncing off a surface
entries.definitionCN: 声音撞上表面后折返的回声，侧重物理回声

entries.definition: of a sound, to be repeated many times as it bounces around a space
entries.definitionCN: 声音在空间里反复反射、久久不绝，比 resonate 更强调多次反射

entries.definition: to share the feelings of another person, especially sadness
entries.definitionCN: 对他人（尤其是不幸）表示同情，侧重立场而非感同身受

normalIntro.en: Resonate is Latin re- plus sonare, to sound, so it is literally sound coming back.
normalIntro.cn: resonate 是拉丁语 re- 加 sonare（发声），字面意思就是「声音折返而来」。

normal.en: The son in resonate is the same son as in sonar and sonic: all of them are about sound.
normal.cn: resonate 中间的 son 与 sonar、sonic 里的 son 相同，都与声音有关。

normal.en: A sonata is a piece played on instruments; the same sound root lies underneath.
normal.cn: sonata 意为「奏鸣曲」，底下也是同一个表示「声音」的词根。

normal.en: Resonate with is the usual partner: the idea resonated with readers.
normal.cn: resonate with 是最常见的搭配：某个想法引起了读者的共鸣。

normal.en: Resonant means full of echo; resonance is the quality of that echo.
normal.cn: resonant 意为「充满回声的」，resonance 则是这种回声的性质。

normal.en: Spelling hook: resonate keeps a single s, so it is not written with a doubled s.
normal.cn: 拼写钩子：resonate 只有一个 s，不要写成双写。

abstract.en: Picture a bell in a stone hall: the strike is over, but the air keeps on ringing.
abstract.cn: 想象石厅里的一口钟：敲击已经结束，空气却还在响。

abstract.en: Think of two wine glasses side by side: sing to one, and the other begins to hum.
abstract.cn: 想象并排的两只酒杯：对其中一只唱歌，另一只也开始轻轻作响。

abstract.en: Hear a sentence that names exactly how you feel, and feel it land inside you: that is resonance of meaning.
abstract.cn: 听到一句话恰好说出了你的感受，并感到它在心里落定：这就是意义上的共鸣。

examples.en: The deep note resonated in the empty hall.
examples.cn: 那低沉的声音在空荡的大厅里回荡。

examples.en: Her speech resonated with students from small towns.
examples.cn: 她的演讲引起了小城镇学生的共鸣。

examples.en: Songs from that album still resonate with people of every age.
examples.cn: 那张专辑里的歌至今仍能引起各个年龄段的人共鸣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞声内特」——瑞声在墙内特别响：回响、共鸣。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sonare（发声）+ 前缀 re-（回）→ resonare（回响）；派生 resonantia（共鸣），经法语进入英语，核心义「声音折返而来、遥相呼应」。

sensesIntro.en: Resonate starts with a physical ringing sound, becomes a vibration between objects with the same frequency, and then moves into feelings and ideas that answer each other.
sensesIntro.cn: resonate 先指实体声音的回响，再指同频物体之间的振动，最后移到相互呼应的情感与想法上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a struck tuning fork rings on, and a second fork of the same pitch begins to hum.
core.cn: 核心意象：被敲响的音叉余音不止，旁边同音高的音叉也开始轻声作响。

branches.en: The plain physical ring of a sound is the literal beginning.
branches.cn: 声音本身的回响是最字面的起点。

branches.en: Physics explains why matching frequencies make a body answer.
branches.cn: 物理学解释了为什么相同的频率会让物体应和。

branches.en: Words that speak to experience make the listener vibrate in return.
branches.cn: 说到经历深处的话语，会让听者反过来振动。

branches.en: What matters keeps returning to the mind, like an echo.
branches.cn: 重要的事会像回声一样不断回到心里。

branches.en: Emotional resonance and fitting together are two versions of one harmony.

intro.en: Resonate is formed from the Latin prefix re-, the Latin root sonare, and the English verb ending -ate.
intro.cn: resonate 由拉丁语前缀 re-、拉丁语词根 sonare 以及英语动词词尾 -ate 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin sonare means to sound, and with re- it becomes resonare, to sound again and again.
